functions.name: Album / Connect
functions.description: Family photo updates are entered through an album overview, then read and acknowledged inside a per-member gallery.

steps.title: Open a family member's update stream
steps.body: The Album tab now begins with member cards, so the walkthrough should start from choosing whose recent photo updates to open.
steps.mockAction: Tap the Grace card from the Album overview.
steps.expectedEffect: The interface opens Grace's member-specific gallery detail view.

steps.title: Browse one shared moment without entering chat
steps.body: The gallery detail keeps the update lightweight: the photo, timestamp, and note are visible together without requiring an immediate reply.
steps.mockAction: Scroll into the first photo card and read the attached note.
steps.expectedEffect: The user can absorb the update as a quiet family moment rather than a conversational task.

steps.title: Shift the gallery time window
steps.body: The updated detail screen includes a compact time filter, allowing users to check only today's, last week's, last month's, or last year's posts.
steps.mockAction: Open the Last Week dropdown to inspect the available time ranges.
steps.expectedEffect: The range menu expands over the gallery and narrows the visible update set.

steps.title: Respond with a low-pressure reaction
steps.body: Acknowledgement is handled through a lightweight emoji tray rather than a full message composer, which keeps the response burden intentionally small.
steps.mockAction: Tap the reaction button on the photo card to open the emoji tray.
steps.expectedEffect: A short row of emoji reactions appears above the card for quick acknowledgement.

steps.title: Start a self-upload in one step
steps.body: When the current user opens their own album, the camera button leads directly to a simple capture-source sheet instead of a complex upload flow.
steps.mockAction: Tap the camera icon in the top-right corner of the current user's gallery.
steps.expectedEffect: A bottom sheet offers Camera and Library as the first upload choices.

functions.name: Jar
functions.description: Jar now combines a private mood-recording flow with a shared-status care view and animated candy-drop feedback.

steps.title: Start today's mood check-in
steps.body: The updated Jar flow begins from a single plus action, framed as adding one mood candy rather than filling in a heavy diary entry.
steps.mockAction: Tap the plus button beside the 'Add your own mood candy?' prompt.
steps.expectedEffect: The user moves into the day-level editor for a new mood candy entry.

steps.title: Review moods through a private calendar
steps.body: The calendar popup makes it explicit that the full mood history belongs to the current user, while still supporting flexible return visits across different dates.
steps.mockAction: Open 'See calendar' and scan the current month's recorded candies.
steps.expectedEffect: A private monthly calendar appears, showing days with mood candies and allowing date-based revisit.

steps.title: Set visibility before saving
steps.body: The editor now foregrounds privacy control through Private, Soft Share, and Full Share options before the mood candy is saved.
steps.mockAction: Choose a mood, optionally add one sentence, then compare the three share modes.
steps.expectedEffect: The user can decide how much family members see before the candy drops into the jar.

steps.title: Expose only shared status in care view
steps.body: The care popup now clearly separates private mood history from what relatives may gently see, preventing over-exposure while preserving care signals.
steps.mockAction: Open 'Care for someone' and inspect the shared-status card for Mom.
steps.expectedEffect: The popup shows only the shareable status layer and withholds the private calendar.

functions.name: Weekly Echo
functions.description: Weekly Echo now unfolds across three carousel boards and a separate keepsake reveal scene.

steps.title: Read the weekly summary board
steps.body: The first Weekly Echo board consolidates connected days, small moments, and activity counts into one compact weekly reading surface.
steps.mockAction: Open Echo and land on the first board without any extra navigation.
steps.expectedEffect: The user sees the headline weekly recap and the four activity counters together.

steps.title: Scan the small-moments recap
steps.body: The second board shifts from totals to plain-language recap points, letting the week be reviewed as a sequence of gentle moments rather than raw records.
steps.mockAction: Move to the Small Moments board using the carousel controls.
steps.expectedEffect: A short numbered list explains how the week's activity traveled home.

steps.title: Review what the pet kept from the week
steps.body: The third board turns collected traces into categories of shared keepsakes and ends with a clear reveal action for the weekly reward.
steps.mockAction: Advance to the Shared Keepsakes board and inspect the weekly categories.
steps.expectedEffect: The interface summarizes small items and presents the reveal button for this week's keepsake.

steps.title: Open the keepsake reveal scene
steps.body: The reveal button now transitions into a separate scene with a tap-to-open gift box, making the weekly reward feel like the outcome of accumulated small care.
steps.mockAction: Tap 'Reveal This Week's Keepsake' to enter the gift scene.
steps.expectedEffect: A dedicated keepsake screen appears with the closed weekly gift box.

steps.title: Claim the unlocked keepsake
steps.body: Once the box opens, the reward card explains what was unlocked and offers a direct add-to-inventory action without extra navigation.
steps.mockAction: Tap the gift box, wait for the reveal, then focus the claim button.
steps.expectedEffect: The unlocked keepsake card appears with the 'Add to Toy Box' action.
